headline: India says Sheikh Hasina's extradition will be settled legally
summary: The Indian government maintains that any extradition is a legal matter and will be processed according to the law.
details: The Indian government has stated that the extradition of former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will be settled through legal processes. This comes after the Bangladesh government formally requested her return.
Sheikh Hasina fled to India on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising. She has remained in India since then.
In a recent telephone interview with Reuters, Sheikh Hasina expressed her desire to return to Bangladesh in December, stating she must return regardless of the outcome.
When asked about her safe return and discussions with the Bangladesh government, Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal did not provide a direct answer.
Jaiswal emphasized that any extradition is a legal matter and will be resolved according to the law, adding that India's stance on the former Prime Minister has not changed.
The briefing also addressed concerns regarding Indian development projects in Bangladesh, with Jaiswal stating that cooperation projects will continue based on mutual discussions.
caption:
Will Sheikh Hasina return to Bangladesh? India says her extradition is a legal matter to be settled by law.

The Indian government has stated that the extradition of former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will be settled through legal processes. This comes after the Bangladesh government formally requested her return.

Sheikh Hasina fled to India on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising. She has remained in India since then.

In a recent telephone interview with Reuters, Sheikh Hasina expressed her desire to return to Bangladesh in December, stating she must return regardless of the outcome.

When asked about her safe return and discussions with the Bangladesh government, Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal did not provide a direct answer.

Jaiswal emphasized that any extradition is a legal matter and will be resolved according to the law, adding that India's stance on the former Prime Minister has not changed.

The briefing also addressed concerns regarding Indian development projects in Bangladesh, with Jaiswal stating that cooperation projects will continue based on mutual discussions.

headline: HSC examinees resume protest in front of parliament after police dispersal
summary: Students are demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon over exam scheduling during floods and alleged question errors.
details: Protesting HSC examinees gathered again in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban on Manik Mia Avenue on Tuesday night, hours after being dispersed by police.
The renewed protest disrupted vehicular movement between Asad Gate and the Khamarbari area, prompting police to arrange alternative routes to minimize public suffering.
Earlier in the evening, police reportedly used baton charges to disperse students who refused to leave the parliament complex area.
The demonstrators are demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon, citing severe flooding and waterlogging during examinations.
Students also highlighted alleged errors in question papers and criticized remarks reportedly made by the minister regarding the examinees.
Earlier on Tuesday afternoon, the students had also blocked the Science Lab intersection to reiterate their demands.
While students claim police used force, an official from Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station denied the use of batons, stating students left on their own.
caption:
HSC students return to the parliament area just hours after police dispersed them. They are demanding the Education Minister's resignation.

Protesting HSC examinees gathered again in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban on Manik Mia Avenue on Tuesday night, hours after being dispersed by police.

The renewed protest disrupted vehicular movement between Asad Gate and the Khamarbari area, prompting police to arrange alternative routes to minimize public suffering.

Earlier in the evening, police reportedly used baton charges to disperse students who refused to leave the parliament complex area.

The demonstrators are demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon, citing severe flooding and waterlogging during examinations.

Students also highlighted alleged errors in question papers and criticized remarks reportedly made by the minister regarding the examinees.

Earlier on Tuesday afternoon, the students had also blocked the Science Lab intersection to reiterate their demands.

While students claim police used force, an official from Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station denied the use of batons, stating students left on their own.
